messages:
maria-privacy: Quick flag — we received a DSAR via support@ asking for deletion confirmation and proof that ephemeral embeddings used in a past demo were purged. They attached a screenshot referencing a demo customer email. Need a quick plan: do we treat this as a standard DSAR erasure or a retention-exception path? @samir-security @anna-legal

samir-security: Can you paste the request (redacted)? If it's only demo data and not linked to a real person maybe low-risk, but treat conservatively. @kevin-ops can you scan EU dedicated clusters for any matching IDs?

maria-privacy: Paste (redacted):
```
Subject: Request for deletion
I am requesting deletion of all personal data associated with john.doe@example.com used in your demo on 2024-06-10. Attached screenshot of chat output.
Regards, J.
```

kevin-ops: Quick check: found one vector id `embed_12345` in `eu-dedicated-01` embeddings index tied to user_id `user_9876`. Created 2024-06-11. Backups exist (s3://redwood-backups/eu/2024-06-12.tar.gz). I can run targeted delete, but recommend coordinating a KMS key rotation so old key material isn't able to decrypt if backups are persistent. Also need to record audit entries.

anna-legal: If the requester asserts they're the data subject we follow DSAR erasure steps. Confirm identity (reply with last 4 of phone/email or signed doc). Log everything. If backups can't be redacted immediately we document a retention-exception and an expected purge window.

samir-security: Proposed plan: 1) Verify identity, 2) snapshot IDs for audit, 3) run targeted deletion on embeddings index via our internal delete endpoint, 4) optionally rotate KMS keys, 5) if backups still contain data mark retention-exception with timeline. Also we should tighten RBAC: require two approvers for `embeddings.delete` and `keystore.rotate`. Thoughts?

deploy-bot: Incident ticket CREATED: INC-2024-0456 assigned to kevin-ops; severity: low. Link: https://tickets.example/INC-2024-0456

kevin-ops: I'll run the delete and rotate keys. Command I'll run (dry-run first):
```bash
curl -X POST https://internal.api/embeddings/delete -d '{"ids":["embed_12345"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN'
```
Then rotate KMS: `kms.rotate_key --id projects/eu/keystore-main`
I'll schedule backup purge job (cron) after legal confirms: `0 3 * * Sun` with a dry-run one week before.

maria-privacy: Please attach audit log entries and include an `erasure_manifest.json` in the ticket showing which artifacts were deleted vs pending. If we need a retention-exception, note exact data sets and timeframe. @anna-legal can you confirm acceptable timeframe?

anna-legal: Confirmed: treat as PI. Proceed with DSAR flow after identity verification. If backups can't be immediately cleaned, retention-exception is acceptable but must include a max remediation window (we propose 30 days) and stakeholder notification.

samir-security: I'll open a PR to add 2-approver RBAC on `embeddings.delete` and `keystore.rotate` and enable mandatory audit logging on the delete endpoint. Example audit call: `audit.log('embeddings.delete', user, ids)` — will link PR in the ticket.

kevin-ops: Completed steps: deleted `embed_12345`, started KMS rotation, and recorded audit event. Audit snippet: `audit: {"action":"embeddings.delete","user":"kevin-ops","ids":["embed_12345"],"ts":2398765450}` — attaching to INC-2024-0456. Backups scheduled for purge, dry-run next Sun.

maria-privacy: Thanks team. I'll keep the requester updated with the expected timeline and close loop once legal signs off. :thumbsup:
